Hi team — draft NIST mapping is attached (tabbed by NIST function: Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover). High-level notes for the RFP response:

- Identify: asset inventory (models + weights catalog), model cards stored in internal registry (auto-generated metadata).
- Protect: encrypted model storage (KMS integration), access control (RBAC + audit trails), tenant isolation for dedicated deployments.
- Detect: anomaly detection for input distribution drift + token-level latency/quality alerts.
- Respond: automated rollback + canary rollback policies; incident triage playbooks.
- Recover: point-in-time model snapshots and deterministic deployment artifacts for repro.

For the evaluation/regression section I propose we include the following concrete artifacts:
1) Eval_Regression_Playbook_v2.md — baseline/regression test corpus, acceptance thresholds (per-task metrics), pre/post-deploy A/B holdback configuration.
2) CI pipeline integration notes (how we gate model version rollouts).
3) Example test set anonymization process and synthetic augmentation approach for regulated PII datasets.

Evelyn — could you confirm the monitoring cadence and alert thresholds we typically recommend for financial workloads (sensitivity to false positives is important here)? I’ve attached the working spreadsheet: Redwood_NIST_RMF_Mapping.xlsx.

Thanks — adding security/compliance specifics and the eval/regression approach. Key points to include in the RFP response:

1) EU AI Act positioning
- For the typical GenAI text-completion and chat endpoints used by GlobalBank, the product is not intrinsically a "high-risk" AI system under Article 6 unless used in a way that falls into the enumerated high-risk categories (e.g., automated credit scoring, critical public services). We will explicitly document intended use and customer responsibilities in the MPR (model processing records).
- We provide controls and documentation to support customers who treat their deployments as high-risk: risk assessment templates, Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) support, transparency logs, model cards and datasets metadata.

2) NIST AI RMF mapping (operational controls) — short checklist to include in RFP
- Governance: formal owner for model risk, model acceptance board, periodic attestation cadence (quarterly).
- Metrics: performance, fairness probes where applicable, robustness (adversarial fuzzing) results retained per model version.

3) Eval/Regression approach (concrete)
- Pre-deploy: unit + integration tests in CI, benchmark run using a held-out holdback set, metric thresholds (ROUGE/BLEU/F1 or embed-sim depending on task) with per-model baselines.
- Rolling canary: deploy to 5% of traffic for 24–72 hours with automatic rollback if key metrics degrade >5% relative to baseline or if latency SLA breach occurs.
- Continuous monitoring: daily aggregated quality checks (sampled prompts), drift detection (KS-test on embedding distribution), and weekly regression reports.
- Human-in-the-loop alerts: when high-severity quality regressions occur, route to CS+Solutions with a defined SLA for investigation (24–48h initial triage).
- For regulated PII datasets: synthetic augmentation + k-anonymity checks before including in test sets; access to redacted audit logs for customers.

4) Evidence and artifacts we will provide
- Redwood_NIST_RMF_Mapping.xlsx (control mapping)
- EU_Act_Positioning_Summary.pdf (executive summary for legal/procurement)
- Eval_Regression_Playbook_v2.md (runbook with steps, CI examples, alerts)

I’ve attached the Playbook draft and PDF summary. Let me know if procurement wants us to include SOC2 control IDs or a KMS architecture diagram — we can provide both.
